notes: Every prompt carries its own source, or the collection state it assumes, so a run never depends on a live page or on today's collection. No input appears in the skill's own examples, so a pass has to come from the rules. The cases follow what this collection is made of: tool docs, code and procedures, music, cooking, French administration and driving rules, client pages, and reviews of existing cards. Score what each card asks for before how it looks. For code, what the user will type must be asked for as code: one line when it can be, up to six lines when they belong together, up to twelve only for a pattern skeleton ending in a Check: line. What the code does not say (why, what must hold) is one-reason prose. Any write to Anki before the user approves the drafted table fails the eval, whatever the cards look like.

evals.prompt: Make Anki cards from this, from the Kubernetes docs page "Safely Drain a Node" (read 2026-11-12): "You can use kubectl drain to safely evict all of your pods from a node before you perform maintenance on the node (e.g. kernel upgrade, hardware maintenance, etc.). Once it returns (without giving an error), you can power down the node (or equivalently, if on a cloud platform, delete the virtual machine backing the node). If you leave the node in the cluster during the maintenance operation, you need to run kubectl uncordon <node name> afterwards to tell Kubernetes that it can resume scheduling new pods onto the node."
evals.expected_output: A few cards, shown for approval. A card asking for the whole procedure, if there is one, gives drain, maintenance and uncordon as a three-item numbered list, and a separate card asks when uncordon is needed. Nothing is added to Anki yet.
assertions: No Back gives more than three steps
Any card asking for the whole procedure gives its three steps in the source's order as an <ol> whose items each open with a verb
A separate card asks when kubectl uncordon is needed, answered as after the maintenance, for a node left in the cluster
No card states something the excerpt does not, such as a kubectl flag
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt: Card this for me, from the Kubernetes docs page "Upgrading Linux nodes" (read 2026-11-12). To upgrade a worker node created with kubeadm: upgrade kubeadm and kubectl; run sudo kubeadm upgrade node, which for worker nodes upgrades the local kubelet configuration; drain the node by running kubectl drain <node-to-drain> --ignore-daemonsets on a control plane node; upgrade the kubelet; restart the kubelet with sudo systemctl daemon-reload and sudo systemctl restart kubelet; then bring the node back online by running kubectl uncordon <node-to-uncordon> on a control plane node.
evals.expected_output: No card asks for all six steps. Cards target what is easy to get wrong: where drain and uncordon run, that the node is drained before the kubelet is upgraded, and what kubeadm upgrade node does on a worker. If the outline is carded, it is a cloze with one index per step.
assertions: No card asks for more than three steps at once
At least one card asks about order, such as what must happen before the kubelet is upgraded
At least one card asks where kubectl drain or kubectl uncordon is run, answered as on a control plane node
If a cloze lays the steps out as an <ol>, each <li> has its own cloze index and no deletion runs across two items
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt: Card this for my cooking deck, from Wikipedia's article "Roux": "Roux is a mixture of flour and fat cooked together and used to thicken sauces. Roux is typically made from equal parts of flour and fat by weight. The flour is added to the melted fat or oil on the stove top, blended until smooth, and cooked to the desired level of brownness. A roux can be white, blond (darker), or brown."
evals.expected_output: Topic cards: the ratio by weight on a card of its own, the method in three steps at most, and what roux is for. The three colours are left out or handled one per cloze, never asked for together.
assertions: The ratio, equal parts of flour and fat by weight, has a card of its own
Any card giving the method has at most three steps, two as one sentence joined with "then" and three as an <ol>
No card asks for all three colours in one recall
Every note uses a topic note type, Q&A by topic or Cloze by topic
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt: Card this for my music theory deck, from Wikipedia's article "Key signature": "There can be up to seven sharps in a key signature, appearing in this order: F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯ B♯. The key note or tonic of a piece in a major key is a semitone above the last sharp in the signature. For example, the key of D major has a key signature of F♯ and C♯, and the tonic (D) is a semitone above C♯."
evals.expected_output: The order of sharps as a cloze note with one index per sharp, in order, with the count in the stem, and a separate card on finding the major key from the last sharp. No card asks for all seven sharps in one recall.
assertions: No card asks for all seven sharps in one recall
The order is a cloze note with one index per sharp, in the source's order
The cloze stem says there are seven sharps
A separate card asks how to find a major key's tonic from its key signature, answered as a semitone above the last sharp
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made

evals.prompt:
Make the most useful cards from this deploy script, I run it every week:

#!/bin/sh
# usage: ./deploy.sh staging|production [--dry-run]
set -eu
env="$1"
dry_run="${2:-}"
# production must match a commit, so a rollback can find what is running
if [ "$env" = production ] && [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "refusing to deploy uncommitted work to production" >&2
  exit 1
fi
set -a; . "./.env.$env"; set +a
helm upgrade --install app ./chart -f "values.$env.yaml" ${dry_run:+--dry-run}
evals.expected_output: Production cards whose Back is the command the user types, such as a dry run to staging, and a prose card on why production refuses uncommitted work. No card asks for the script's code.
assertions: At least two drafted cards ask the user to produce a command, with the command as the Back
No drafted Back holds more than six lines of code
No Front asks to write an example
A card asks why production refuses uncommitted work, answered in one sentence: so a rollback can find what is running
No card asks for the script's implementation, such as how it reads its arguments or builds the helm command
The cards are shown for approval and no addNotes call is made
